entry.title: Fed governor Ana Hale backs one more rate cut this year
entry.summary: the fictional governor said cooling inflation leaves room for one more quarter-point cut before December.

entry.title: Lumen Labs releases an open AI model that runs on a laptop
entry.summary: the fictional lab published weights for a small model it says matches last year's large models on coding tests.

entry.title: Orbita launches 40 broadband satellites on a reused booster
entry.summary: the fictional launch company flew the booster for a ninth time and landed it at sea.

entry.title: Pell County reports its largest measles outbreak in a decade
entry.summary: health officials in the fictional county confirmed 41 cases, most in unvaccinated children.

entry.title: Appeals court pauses a state law requiring app-store age checks
entry.summary: the court said the fictional law likely burdens free speech while the case continues.

entry.title: Qaldar raises oil output by 200,000 barrels a day
entry.summary: the fictional producer said it will raise exports from next month to win back market share.

entry.title: Pentagon picks two firms to build drone-interceptor prototypes
entry.summary: the fictional contracts fund 50 low-cost interceptors for testing next year.

entry.title: China adds two battery minerals to its export license list
entry.summary: in this fictional scenario, exporters of two minerals used in batteries will need permits from next month.

entry.title: Fern raises $60M to offer rooftop solar leases to renters
entry.summary: the fictional startup will pay landlords to host panels and sell power to tenants.

entry.title: Voltline recalls 80,000 e-bikes over battery fires
entry.summary: the fictional maker says owners should stop charging the bikes indoors until they get a free battery swap.

entry.title: EU fines Pinecone $1.1 billion over default search deals
entry.summary: regulators say the fictional tech giant paid phone makers to keep rivals off home screens.

entry.title: Card following a card id that does not exist
entry.summary: bad card, follows points nowhere.

entry.title: Kestrel humanoids sort parcels without remote operators
entry.summary: the fictional company showed robots working a full shift in a parcel hub with no human teleoperation.

entry.title: Retail sales rose 0.4% in September, fictional survey shows
entry.summary: spending on restaurants and travel led gains while furniture sales fell.

entry.title: Tovu elects its first woman prime minister
entry.summary: the fictional island nation's parliament chose a former finance minister.

entry.title: Lantern-2 probe sends first close images of a comet
entry.summary: the fictional probe passed 800 km from the comet and found jets of water vapor.

entry.title: State high court strikes down Pell County district map
entry.summary: the fictional court ordered a new map before next year's local elections.

entry.title: Northland orders 12 air-defense batteries
entry.summary: the fictional state signed a contract worth $3 billion, its largest arms deal.

entry.title: Grid operator adds record battery storage ahead of winter
entry.summary: the fictional operator says new batteries can power 2 million homes for four hours.

entry.title: US and Maravel open talks on coffee tariffs
entry.summary: the new fictional government asked to cut duties on coffee and cocoa exports.

entry.title: Rail freight volumes hit a two-year high
entry.summary: fictional industry data show carloads up 6% from a year ago.

entry.title: Paper Moons tops the weekend box office
entry.summary: the fictional animated film earned $48 million in its debut.

entry.title: Ten Pacific states agree on joint fishing patrols
entry.summary: the fictional pact shares patrol boats and satellite data against illegal fishing.

entry.title: Deep-sea survey finds 30 new species off Tovu
entry.summary: a fictional expedition logged fish, corals and sponges never described before.
